text: A man who displays his own merit is a coxcomb, and a man who does not know it is a fool. A man of sense knows it, exerts it, avails himself of it, but never boasts of it; and always SEEMS rather to under than over value it, though in truth, he sets the right value upon it.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXX, to his son, London, February 4, Old Style 1751
